Docs.summary: Defines the platform-neutral behavior contract for a handler that manages an .

remarks.para: declares the same child-management members, but it also declares PlatformView using a per-target-framework type alias, which prevents an external platform backend from implementing it. This interface carries the behavior without the alias.

The two interfaces are intentionally unrelated: is untouched, so existing implementations and callers keep working. A handler that implements the members as ordinary public methods — as the in-box does — satisfies both interfaces at once.
Because is covariant, ILayoutHandler<object> matches any layout handler regardless of backend.

How .NET MAUI Controls reaches a layout handler. Microsoft.Maui.Controls.Layout does not cast to either layout interface. It raises the child-management operations as command mapper keys — Handler.Invoke(nameof(ILayoutHandler.Add), new LayoutHandlerUpdate(index, view)) and so on — which is type-agnostic and therefore reaches an external backend's handler exactly as it reaches the in-box one. Referencing for its member names is always allowed; only implementing it is blocked. An external backend should use those same key strings so Controls interop keeps working.

Known gap. The obsolete Microsoft.Maui.Controls.Compatibility.Layout<T>.LayoutHandler property is declared as and evaluates Handler as ILayoutHandler, so it returns for a handler that implements only this generic interface. It is the sole runtime cast to left in .NET MAUI, it is a public convenience property that no in-box code path reads, and its declaring type is [Obsolete] — so it does not affect layout behavior. It is called out here because this interface is, for that legacy property specifically, a compile-time contract only.
